This caused the decrease of elongation when the alloy was stretched at 300 °C.

The higher tensile temperature promoted the coarsening of GBPs, causing the formation of PFZs. Meanwhile, the increasing recrystallization textures meant that more grains were in soft orientation. These two factors contributed to the increase of elongations from room temperature to 250 °C.

As the tensile temperature increased, the coarsening of T1 phases decreased the precipitation strengthening of the alloy, and the decreasing deformation textures and the increasing recrystallization textures led to the lower average Taylor factor and texture strengthening.
As the temperature reached 300 °C, the ledge mechanism was activated and a lateral diffusion process of solutes became accessible.
T1 phases hindered dislocation slip and improved the strength by the shearing mechanism and the Orowan bypass mechanism.
